posts.text: JUST IN: 🇺🇸🇨🇳 US intelligence finds Nvidia $NVDA CEO Jensen Huang had a 'romantic relationship' with a Chinese spy, FT reports.
posts.author: WatcherGuru

posts.text:
BREAKING: US officials believe Nvidia, $NVDA, CEO Jensen Huang had a "romantic relationship" with a Chinese spy from China’s main intelligence agency, per FT.

Details include:

1. US officials say Jensen Huang had been romantically involved with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed

2. US intelligence shows that Alice Huang was recruited as a spy by China’s Ministry of State Security

3. Megaspeed has now come under US scrutiny for allegedly smuggling advanced Nvidia chips into China

It's unclear what the implications of this development will be.

posts.text:
I’ve used the $axon formerly Taser $TASR as an analogy of what I think could happen to $Hg $hgraf as it becomes a mainstream success.  

At Sprott we became the largest investor in the company as @ericnuttall was a young analyst tasked with following Eric Sprott’s  of simply looking through companies reported earnings everyday and highlighting / digging into ones that reported significant growth in sales over two quarters and on the cusp of turning cash flow and earnings positive.  

Young Mr. Nuttall would read out the names of companies, brief description of what they do and the quarter over quarter improvements in their revenue and earnings our morning meetings.   

Eric would then say… ‘do more work on that one’.  Often assigning the task to a specialist in the companies category or asking Nuttall to dig in himself and model it.  Back then we had a small team and a couple of us had to act as special sits analysts along with covering a sector or for me, technical analysis of our portfolio and the over all market. 

After a bit of work it on Taser we gained the belief the tech was safe and that it would be utilized by military, police, security guards and home security in a huge way.  With not just headline sales of the taser guns but with a massive recurring revenue stream from cartridges.  They also had an extremely talented R&D team and planned to go into all sorts of non-lethal weapons. 

The stock had an incredible journey….

First Move (+4,900%): Surging due to police adoption of the stun guns paired with aggressive short covering propelled TASR on a roughly +4,900% run (~50×) from late-2002 lows to its peak in late 2004.

Second Move (−75% to −88%): Regulatory inquiries, safety lawsuits, and coordinated short-seller attacks caused the stock to collapse by 75% in 2005, eventually reaching a maximum drawdown of approximately −88%.

This was all pure bullshit.  The science was sound and you had to be a special kinda dumb to argue that it’s better to shoot someone with a bullet rather than taser them when they run at police wielding a knife. Or beat them with a baton when they won’t let you cuff them because they are whacked on hard drugs.

Truth of the science prevailed and the global adoption of the tech with recurring revenue prevailed. 

Third Move (+10,000% to +20,000%+): Rebranding to Axon Enterprise and transforming into a high-margin public-safety ecosystem through body cameras and cloud software drove a massive +10,000% to +20,000%+ surge (100–200×+) from its post-crash trough to the 2025 all-time highs.

I’ve used this analogy since day one on $hg $hgraf because I thought it’s going to have a similar journey. 

Anytime we get a massive run in an emerging company like we had from 20c to $11 or +50x you just know shortsellers will come.  Seeking to scare people into taking profits and they are joined by hedgefunds that love volatility and reversion to the mean trading. 

These sorts will make every arguement possible to say the company won’t succeed.  Safety is a big one. And we saw the same thing with $hg as the short sellers said they won’t get EPA approval for 5 years if every.  Meanwhile 6 months later they got EU Reach, UK and EPA to both produce and sell their graphene.  They’ve made their attacks and have been proven wrong.  But all the attacks likely contributed to the recent declines. Claims that there will be no sales etc have shaken peoples confidence.  

So, here we sit… In my mind very similar to the big declines Tasr had as the short attacked.   Now it’s show time.   The squeeze that will be coming will be epic if the company delivers on orders to the extent that management has guided.  

When you look back on the axon charge that initial decline is a tiny blip filling the great success they’ve had up to the recent highs. 

Looking at its recent decline today actually makes me want to dig in and see if is a buy.  Great company and management team. 

Due your own due diligence, no advice here
